summary: Cut at 7.4. The scores so far are 6.5, 6.9 and 7.1 (cut), then 7.3 and 7.4 in the revival, and now 7.4 again. Caiman is 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. This is the revival's last round, so a score below 7.5 is a cut. Every lost-wax gate is green at draft (768 x 320) and export (1536 x 448), and the template gate passes. Round 5's punch items were all attempted. Two of them pass. The eyes are now smooth domes, each with a brow over its top third and a short slit pupil, and in head-hero.png and hero.png they read as eyes, with no coffee bean. The crest in side.png and hero.png is a comb of thin, separate, tall spines, the best tuatara cue the ring has had. Two items fail, and the first one matters most. (1) The stone still reads as the eye. It is now 2.0 mm, flush, and on the skull midline 5 mm behind the eyes. From above (head.png, face.png) it is a correct parietal jewel. But the eyes moved forward to the snout end. In every three-quarter and profile view (hero.png, hero-300, head-hero.png, stones.png, bare-vs-finished.png), the stone's bright rimmed green disc lands on the visible flank of the head, exactly where a lizard's eye sits. The real eyes then read as nostril bulbs or a frog's eyes on the tip of the snout. At 300 px the first read is still 'lizard with a green eye', and that breaks Logan's rule that the stone is never an eye. Round 5's acceptance test ('no view shows the stone at the cheek level where an eye sits') fails in four of the views. (2) The tail's rim edge in reverse.png is still a regular grid of pyramid studs, row after row, and the middle of the tail in palm.png still has a run of squared blocks. Seen from above, stones.png still shows the back crest as a file of dark square pyramids, because the thin blades only read in silhouette. The gain on the eyes and crest is cancelled by the new eye-and-stone geometry, so the score holds at 7.4 and does not reach 7.5. A further revival would need the stone to leave the head's visible flank in three-quarter view; the punch list records how.
strengths: One animal from face to palm: the head on the face, the nape crest and front legs at the shoulders, the hind legs and an S-curved tapering tail across the palm (hero.png, side.png, palm.png). No other Cataphracta ring is as readable as a creature.
The crest is now a comb of thin, separated, tapering spines, tallest at the nape. In side.png and hero.png the serrated outline is the most tuatara-like thing the ring has had.
The eyes are fixed. Each is a smooth 2.0 mm dome with a brow over its top third and one short slit pupil, crisp in head-hero.png and hero.png. Nothing reads as a bean, a clove or a claw.

The 2.0 mm peridot is flush with the skin, on the midline, behind the eyes, and ringed by a narrow rim with the granules carried up to it. From above (head.png, face.png) it is clearly a jewel set in the skull roof, not an eye.
The head skin is graded fine granules, with larger plates over the skull. The body has keeled scales and tubercles, and the toed feet grip the rim. Large, medium and small forms are all present.
Every gate is green, and they match report.json and template-verification.json.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: One tuatara wraps the band from the snout on the face to the tail tip on the far side face, and nothing else is on the band (hero.png, side.png, palm.png).

checklist.item: Hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and contact-300 read as a spiny lizard or iguana with a green eye. The flush stone is still the first round form on the head's visible flank in three-quarter view, and the real eyes at the snout tip read as nostrils. The comb crest helps in side.png, but 'tuatara' still needs the caption.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The eyes, brows, slit pupils, beak notch, toes and spines render crisp in head-hero.png, hero.png and side.png. The seat rim is clean, with no radial combing. There is minor granule smearing on the thighs in face.png, but no combing.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The 2.0 mm peridot sits flush in a gypsy seat (2.8 mm, GypsyMound) with a burnished rim, and it is visible in every view of the face. stones.json: 1 stone, crowding 0, tight pairs 0.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The head, body, legs and tail are rounded and tapered. The remaining mechanical passages are the stud grid along the tail's rim edge (reverse.png) and the square-pyramid file of the crest seen from above (stones.png). They are not enough to fail the item, but they cost score.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: This is a procedural Flat band, not factory stock. Its flattened sides keep a crisp wall-to-face edge wherever the band is plain (bare-vs-finished.png).

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: It is the only figure-on-plain-band composition in either set, and the bladed crest breaks the outline in side.png.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large forms: the body, head and tail. Medium: the legs, eyes, crest and stone. Small: the granules, scales and toes. The figure is as dense as Caiman and more legible. Half the band is deliberately plain.

gates.claimed: Castable under lost wax at the 0.8 mm fill
gates.verified: The verdict is 'Castable' (not 'with care'), process LostWax, thinnest wall 2.134 mm, at draft and export. The two-part undercut notes are informational.

gates.gate: land_widths: every section under 0.8 mm named with its bench treatment
gates.verified: all_named is true and removed is []. At export, area_named 23.24 mm² equals area_under_floor 23.24 mm². This is up from 7.24 mm² in round 5: the comb accounts for 12.71 mm² (thinnest 0.111 mm), and the parietal seat lip for 2.92 mm² at 0.0002 mm (it was 0.006 mm² in round 5). Every note names its bench treatment, and the seat lip is burnished over the girdle. That passes the gate, but the flush seat now leaves a knife-edge lip about 500 times larger in area for the setter to burnish.

gates.gate: Ray release 0 obstructions / 0 unresolved at 0.100 and 0.075 mm
gates.verified: two_part_numbers status is NotApplicable, with 0 unresolved rays at both pitches. At export there are 384 obstructions at 0.100 mm and 518 at 0.075 mm, reported but not gated under lost wax. The undercut is 59.6 of 1336.3 mm² (4.46%), worst -67.4 deg, all from 'Tuatara'.
There is no clamp layer: this is lost wax with min_draft_deg 0. The layers are 'Tuatara' and 'Parietal peridot'.

punch_list.zone: The head in three-quarter view: the stone at stone_t 12.0 on the midline (theta 90 deg, seat v 5.44 mm), and the eyes at EYE_X 1.75 near the snout
punch_list.change: Get the stone off the head's visible flank. Either move it back about 3 mm more, onto the nape between the jaw joints and behind the widest part of the skull (so the skull's side slope hides it in hero.png), or drop it into a 0.3 mm countersunk recess with a granulated collar so its rim stops flashing. Also bring the eyes back about 1.0 mm (EYE_X about 2.75) so that 3.5 to 4 mm of beaked snout runs ahead of them and they sit where a lizard's eye sits.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png, hero-300.png and stones.png the topmost round form on the head's near side is the domed eye, with snout ahead of it. The green stone shows only as a disc on the skull roof or nape, above and behind the eye line, and it never sits on the cheek. A viewer of hero-300 says 'lizard with a jewel on its head', not 'green eye'.

punch_list.zone: The tail's rim edge on the palm, theta about 200 to 340 deg (reverse.png); the tail centre on the palm (palm.png)
punch_list.change: The round 5 item was not met. Replace the grid there with jittered, overlapping, domed scales: stagger alternate rings by half a scale, jitter the cell centres by 15%, and lower the scale points by 60% (not 40%) where the tail crosses the rim fillet.
punch_list.acceptance: In reverse.png no run of matching pyramids lines up for more than 3 scales in any direction. In palm.png no squared block rows show along the tail's centre.

punch_list.zone: Dorsal comb from the nape to the hips, as seen from above (stones.png, head.png)
punch_list.change: From above, the blades read as square pyramids with dark gaps. Thin each blade's foot across the band to 0.35 mm and lean its tip 15 deg tailward, so the top view shows a line of narrow slanted blades and not squares.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png and head.png the crest reads as a row of thin slanted blades with no square pyramids. In side.png the serrated outline is kept.

punch_list.zone: The parietal seat lip (land_widths 'the parietal seat': 2.92 mm² at 0.0002 mm)
punch_list.change: Bring the knife-edge lip area back toward round 5's 0.006 mm². Give the seat a 0.15 mm bearing shoulder below the skin, so that the lip is a real burnishing wall rather than a feathered edge.
punch_list.acceptance: land_widths 'the parietal seat' is at most 0.5 mm², with its thinnest section at least 0.05 mm, and every other gate stays green.
